rows.title: report-flush slower in chats with 5+ repositories

A queue summed over a burst is not the night's makespan: the floor or the measure is the owner's (settled 2026-10-08: lent-slot replay). 2026-10-06: 2518 min/day in the 24 h to 07:20, 4899 min/day before 2026-10-05 19:00 and 331 after. Night 052f ran exactly 5 night workers from 14:08 to 18:48 with 10-12 queued (fixed cores/2 slots, 2392 min of night-workers waits on 10-05); c4adcbb8 (room admission up to the cores, 18:37) drained it. rows.title: Suites running over the 60 min/day test budget, mostly workers' covering runs
rows.note: 2026-10-10 (night 4c4e): the gap was the measure. The p10 is now per blob of the suite file at the run's head: a suite that grew in the window was judged against its smaller self (quiet-band gap 17-19 % by name, 3-10 % by blob on blobs of 20+ runs). Only a run's part on a free machine (free_spans) is over its floor: the loaded band is parallel runs' price, judged by the slot replay and the night's makespan. Live, suite seconds over their floor read 5851 min in the 24 h to 06:35 by the old measure and 52 by the new (the day before 1977 and 68); test_time_budget's grown and loaded cases are red on the old code. 2026-10-09: 294 min/day (123 chat + 171 w-min) over the p10 floor; 3603 suite-min ran in 24 h (chats 1793, Updater doctor 1056 and the chat 7977deeb 656 of them in runs of 21-151 suites). Fixed a measure bug: the p10 sampled failed runs too (test_consistency 257 of 1025 rc 1 at 0.04 s), so the floor of a covering suite was an early exit; passing runs only now (share/time_budget.py suite_floor, as suite_audit and run-suites' p90 do), gap share 44 % -> 36 %. Left, by load band (memlogd load1 hourly mean): under 10 the gap is 23 % of suite wall, 10-30 28 %, 30+ 48 % (868 of 1319 gap suite-min). The quiet 23 % is p10 against the median of suites that grew in the 7-day window; the load share is the night's workers at the cores (Egor 2026-10-07) and the owner's benchmark (weather, 2026-10-05), with suites' own CPU about 2 of 10 cores. One-off: a flake hunt (fix/doctor-fix-lock-flake, 10-08 06:43-07:25) ran test_doctor_fix 161 times under load it made. Ruled out: sharding (direct runs of the 4 sharded suites add 27 of 1319), slot waits (room only). Measure proposals to the owner in the handoff. 2026-10-08: 450 min/day; worker suites held 618 min in 24 h: 326 in 516 single-suite iteration runs (test_statusline_hooks 87 min, test_llm_limits_grok 78, test_consistency 77, test_night_run 76), 73 in runs of 20+ suites. Per-suite speed is the suite audit's. 2026-10-07: 622 min/day in 24 h. Worker suite runs held 804 min of wall: 305 in runs of 20+ suites (tests/affected over bin/worker-run or run-suites names 20-60), 114 in three -j 1 runs of one day chat's workers (10-06 02:32-03:00, none since). Dearest by runs x time: test_consistency 111 min (81 runs), test_llm_limits_grok 108 (35, median 186 s), test_night_run 70, test_doctor_fix 66; suite speed is the tests area's (harness-tests holds test_daily_cost-worker-run on night 7777). Seen, not fixed: test_run_suites_journal assert 35 (the /bin/bash untrap case) failed once in an 18-suite wave at load ~75 and passed alone. 2026-10-06: 2266 min/day in 24 h, 2115 since 2026-10-05 19:00 (the slow layer of c4adcbb8 already skips test_statusline_hooks, test_worker_pick and test_instruction_gate inside workers). Wall ran 5-20x CPU (test_statusline_hooks 3066 s at 247 s CPU): wave suites at nice 10 under the owner's benchmark, the cause the wait-classes fixer of the same night fixed in e2c3ec43 (one owner per cause file). Seen, not fixed: 12 worker runs of 8-43 suites at -j 1 (320 min in 2 days, the worker's own flag); workers background run-all past the 600 s Bash cap and poll with a fixed sleep 540-590 that overshoots the suite end (counted as tools). Ruled out: double counting of parallel suites (run_split takes the union per run); unattributed worker suites (rows without worker_run were a chat running suites in a worker's worktree).

rows.title: Suite slot wait over its floor of zero

Fixed: run-suites frees its slot once only its last wave suite runs (a single-suite run and a run with a serial tail keep it); test_slots tail case, red on the old code. Left: room waits (87 min in 24 h at 3-4 allowed) are load admission, not the tail. 2026-10-06: 464 min/day in 24 h, 243 since 2026-10-05 19:00. Same cause as wait-run-suites-slot-hogs, owned tonight by the wait-classes fixer (e2c3ec43: no nice 10 while the keyboard is idle); the tail-capacity lever it left open (a slot is a whole run, one queued run waits on another run's last suite) is the remaining one. rows.title: Locks and polls over their floor of zero: mostly background waits on the limits store lock
rows.note: 2026-10-06: 39 min/day in 24 h, 20 since 2026-10-05 19:00. 87 waits (29.7 min, up to 56 s) were on ~/.llm-limits.json.lock, the store lock llm-limits.sh holds over its merge (share/store-lock.sh store_lock_acquire, 240 x 0.25 s). Its writers are the refresh heartbeat, the statusline refresher and the menu; none runs inside a chat or worker tool call. share/time_budget.py budget() still moves every wait row out of tools, so these charge nobody's real wall (blind spot wait-caller-kind). rows.title: worker-spawn-hook slower in chats with 5+ repositories
rows.note: A confound on the repository axis: bin/worker-spawn-hook.sh reads no repository. Its cost was ~40 forks per Agent spawn (printf|grep|sed per brief header, tr, sed, mkdir, rm, a perl shasum) at 145 ms CPU p50, paid most by the orchestrator chats that span the most repositories and spawn under the heaviest load. Fixed: brief headers, worker-model keys, the title, ATTACH, ROUND, GIT-CLEANUP and MD-GUARD are read with builtins, the spawn hash uses sha256sum (shasum fallback), mkdir/rm only when needed; a claudeb spawn with ACCOUNT/MODEL/EFFORT starts no grep/sed/tr/head/cut/shasum/mkdir (tests/test_worker_spawn_attach.sh, red on the old code). route_account (worker-pick) for a brief without ACCOUNT stays, the routing answer itself.

rows.title: english-gate over 50 ms on every tool call
rows.note: Every call paid cat, a cd/dirname subshell and two jq before anything was known; a non-launch Bash call also ran the read-only awk and a sed screen. Fixed: the payload is read with the read builtin (PreToolUse payloads are small), the hook's dir from BASH_SOURCE, one jq gives tool and command/file_path, and the launcher screen runs with builtins before the read-only check. 47 -> 17 ms on a trivial Bash call, 47 -> 26 ms on a non-Markdown Edit (in place, load ~100); a Bash call naming no launcher and no git starts one jq (tests/test_english_gates.sh, red on the old code). Kept: a git call still reads on (aliases).

rows.title: pr-ready-mattermost slower in chats with 5+ repositories
rows.note: A false prefilter: `*gh*` matched every `night` (night-run, night/ branches), so the orchestrator chats (5+ repositories) paid two more jq, the 2k-line journal library and its awk walk on most Bash calls; workers exit at the CLAUDEB_WORKER check (the 1.0 ms side). Fixed: the prefilter needs `gh pr create|ready` past quotes and continuations; 67 -> 13 ms on `night-run report` (tests/test_pr_mattermost.sh, red on the old code). The hook_grows_size row that appeared after launch is the same cause.

rows.title: report-flush over 50 ms on every tool call
rows.note: report-bus started (bash, store-lock, two jq) on every call with nothing queued. Fixed: the hook checks report-bus's own has_pending/over_cap (queue root of shared-invariants row cg) with builtin globs for every session the payload names and starts report-bus only with work or with no session named; 87 -> 7-11 ms on a quiet call (tests/test_report_flush.sh, red on the old code). The payload stays one cat: the read builtin reads a pipe a byte at a time and PostToolUse carries the whole tool response. Closes item 2 of docs/handoffs/2026-10-04-hook-floors.md.

rows.title: worker-run ends the nohup'd jobs of logo-vectorizer-bench builder workers as run orphans, most at the 6 h deadline; the on-purpose detaches stay fixed

Both fixes hold: of 45 orphans 2026-10-07 14:00 to 2026-10-09 03:38, none is session-trash's purge or worker-run's pack. All 45 are logo-vectorizer-bench builder workers' `nohup .venv/bin/python …&` traces and evals (the Bash tool's timeout makes them detach): 26 of 2026-10-09 from three runs the 6 h deadline killed (19, 1, 6), so the rule counts jobs cut with the run, not left behind; 15 from two done runs whose results promised a chain still running or queued last, which end_run_orphans then ended (the false report fixed in llm-legs@6431047f: worker-run report prints ENDED: with the count and commands). 4 more on 2026-10-08 came from a 4 s failed run on the unknown account tronjhon (`llm-limits.sh --refresh-account claude/tron…`, an elevenlabs timeout): who spawns that refresh under the run id is unverified. Counting only self-ended runs, or per command family (blind spot worker-orphans-unclassified), would be a judge change: handoff.

rows.title: eod-sorted-gate stripped quotes from the raw payload with bash 3.2 ${input//…/}, cubic: 2 KB of command took 5 s
rows.note: 2026-10-07: 9 cuts an hour at launch, 32 at the rerun. claude-setup@16f3d32 (night 2026-10-06) screened the raw payload with three ${input//…/} substitutions under /bin/bash 3.2, cubic once the pattern matches: a heredoc command of 1 KB took 1.0 s, 2 KB 4.8 s (the 5 s cut), 4 KB 24 s, 8 KB over 2 min. Fixed: the screen is one linear regex over the raw payload, each word spliced past quotes, backslashes and JSON escapes (hooks/lib/splice.sh, which review-flow-gate's private rf_splice became); 100 KB in 53 ms. Same defect, same fix, under 3 s at 16 KB but unbounded above: comment-gate, commit-report, english-gate (may_launch), pr-ready-mattermost. Test: tests/test_hook_long_command.sh runs the five under /bin/bash on a 16 KB heredoc with a 4 s alarm (red on eod-sorted-gate, comment-gate, english-gate, commit-report old code). Reproduced with the screen alone: a 2 KB heredoc naming no commit, so neither eod_candidates nor the jq state reads were reached.

rows.title: context-nudge did its full work on a trivial Bash call
rows.note: PostToolUse on every tool: jq on the payload, wc, tail|grep for a boundary and tail|jq for the size, whatever the context. Its work is per call by design, so the cut is a ceiling: lib/context-size.jq with `--arg bound 1` also prints the counted usage's output_tokens plus the bytes of its line and every later one; the hook keeps size+that, the transcript size and path in <session>.size, and while no nudge is spent and ceiling + bytes written since + 20000 (CONTEXT_NUDGE_SKIP_MARGIN: reminders and tool schemas Claude Code adds unwritten) stays under stage1 it exits after wc (2 forks instead of 6). A token is at least a byte, so the skip never hides a crossing the transcript shows. Test: test_context_nudge.sh (no tail under the ceiling, red on old; growth that can reach stage1 is read again and nudges). Ruled out: dropping the payload jq (top-level key order is the only other reader) and a time-based throttle (no bound on growth).

rows.title: tests/affected and run-all broke on bash 3.2 and on zsh's unsplit suite list
rows.note: Confirmed: /bin/bash 3.2 cannot parse share/affected-suites.sh line 35 (a case pattern without its leading paren inside $(...)); tests/affected execs PATH bash, so a PATH with /bin first broke it. zsh never splits `$suites`, so run-suites got one newline-joined argument and said 'no such suite'. Fixed: the leading paren, run-suites splits a multi-line suite argument. Ruled out: run-suites itself (it re-execs Homebrew bash).

rows.title: worker-launch-gate's awk died on Cyrillic text and the gate let the call through
rows.note: Confirmed: macOS awk 20200816 in a UTF-8 locale counts bytes in substr() but decodes in a regex match, so a lone byte of a multibyte character dies with 'towc: multibyte conversion failure'; worker-launch-gate's prestrip pipeline then hit '|| exit 0' and skipped its scan. Fixed: LC_ALL=C on the command-text awks of worker-launch-gate, worker-tag-hook, worker-git-guard and share/heredoc-mask. Probed every PreToolUse:Bash hook of claude-setup with five Cyrillic shapes: none printed the error (cd-guard's mask gives the same output in both locales).

rows.title: Suites inherited night-run's live RUN_SUITES_JOURNAL

rows.title: Relays' first worker-run start refused for an ACCOUNT:/MODEL: flag

The gate is right; the fix is the claude-setup agent text, see the handoff. workdir-is-home and NESTED_MODEL_REFUSED were single orchestrator mistakes. 2026-10-08: Fixed: the relay agents pass --account/--model exactly as their prompt's ACCOUNT:/MODEL: lines say and never one it lacks (the gate judges the prompt, worker-run the saved file); test_consistency pins the sentence. It recurred 2026-10-07 02:46 and 05:04 before the fix (row log_audit:worker-launch-gate-account-flag).

rows.title: Relays poll in 9-minute rounds and models sleep-poll throttled jobs

The 110-minute throttle waits are logo-vectorizer-bench's own throttle under load (weather); its 'all busy, 4 of 8 slots open' message belongs to that repository. Night 20261007T213650Z-7b98: kept. worker-run wait returns the moment a run ends, so a longer round saves only Sonnet relay turns, never time, and would slow a SendMessage note to the next round; raising the chats' Bash cap is live settings no branch carries. logo-vectorizer-bench's 'all busy, 4 of 8 slots open' is correct: 4 slots allowed under pressure of 8, all 4 held. rows.title: The edit-conflict notice named a quiet chat as the owner of foreign WIP
rows.note: The chat's own correction says the edit hook named «Updater doctor» because it had been quiet for 44 minutes, while that chat's writes came from a worker in its own worktree; bin/land's attribution was right, and the second wrong claim was an ad-hoc journal query. The component is claude-setup hooks/edit-conflict-notice.sh, handed off. 2026-10-08: Cause: review-flow-gate journaled a Bash write's relative target against the payload cwd, which cd-guard keeps at the session's checkout, so `cd <worktree> && sed -i … bin/x` recorded bin/x in main under that chat. Fixed: rj_command_write_paths resolves against the command's last cd (rj_command_moves) and drops a relative target after an unresolvable cd. claude-setup 7df3337 (rj_write_owner: ownership follows the written content) landed beside it; this fix settles which path a Bash write records.

rows.title: Parallel lanes pinned to one account hit its session wall together
